name: com.loomivoai/loomivo
title: Loomivo: verified local businesses
description: Find verified local businesses worldwide and send them booking, order or quote requests.

tools.name: search_businesses
tools.description: Search verified local businesses on Loomivo by what they do and where. Use this first when the customer has not named a specific business (e.g. 'a dentist in Karaikal'); if they named one, search for its name. Returns up to 20 businesses with their slug (needed by get_business, get_available_times and create_request), type, town, and 'can': what customers can do online ('book', 'order', 'quote'; 'request' for a free listing whose owner confirms within 24 hours; null if not taking requests). Read-only, no side effects. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

query.description: What the customer wants, or the business's name. Words like 'dentist', 'salon', 'seafood restaurant', 'Sea Shell'. May be empty to list everything in a town.

city.description: Town or city name, exact match, any case. Optional.

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Get the owner-verified details of one business by slug (from search_businesses): description, phone, address, opening hours, closed days, services and products with prices, offer ids, stock left, service lengths, how booking works there (by service or by table with party size), whether it confirms instantly, and how the customer pays the business. Call this before get_available_times and create_request: it says which kind of request the business takes ('can') and gives the offer_id / service_id values to send. Read-only, no side effects. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

slug.description: The business's id from search_businesses (the 'slug' field).

tools.name: get_available_times
tools.description: List free booking start times on one date for a business that takes bookings (get_business returns can: 'book'). Use before create_request with kind 'book', and offer the customer only these times. Times are the business's local time. Send service_id so only times where the whole service fits are returned (a 90-minute service needs 90 free minutes); for restaurants that book tables, send party_size. Bookings open up to 14 days ahead. If a date has no times, the reply lists open_days to try instead. Read-only, no side effects. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

slug.description: The business's id from search_businesses (the 'slug' field).

date.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD, in the business's local time; today up to 14 days ahead.

service_id.description: Optional. The id of a service (offer of kind 'service') from get_business; its length decides which times fit.

party_size.description: Optional, for table bookings: the number of people (up to booking.max_party from get_business). Default 2.

staff_id.description: Optional. A person from get_business 'staff' when the customer wants someone specific.

tools.name: create_request
tools.description: Send a booking, order or quote request to a business for the customer. Side effects: saves the request, emails the business owner (and the customer, if customer_email is given), and holds the time for bookings. Always confirm the business, time or items, and the customer's name and phone with the customer before calling. Use kind 'book' with a slot from get_available_times (plus service_id, or party_size for tables); kind 'order' with items [{offer_id, qty}] from get_business and/or details in the customer's words, and fulfilment 'pickup' or 'delivery' (delivery needs address); kind 'quote' with details. Send the kind get_business returns in 'can'. Status in the reply: 'confirmed' (the business confirms instantly), 'new' (the business confirms; check with get_request_status) or 'pending' (waiting up to 24 hours). Returns a ref and status_url; once confirmed, 'pay' says how the customer pays the business directly. Not idempotent: each call creates a new request, so do not retry a call that returned a ref; on an error, read the message, fix the input, then call again. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

slug.description: The business's id from search_businesses (the 'slug' field).

kind.description: What the customer wants: 'book' a time, 'order' products, or a 'quote'. Must match 'can' from get_business.

slot.description: For 'book': the start, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the business's local time, one of get_available_times.

service_id.description: For 'book': the service booked (from get_business); its length decides how long the booking is.

party_size.description: For 'book' at a restaurant that books tables: the number of people.

staff_id.description: For 'book': optional, a specific person from get_business 'staff'.

items.description: For 'order': products picked from get_business offers (in stock only).

qty.description: How many (not more than 'left' when given).

fulfilment.description: For 'order': pickup at the business or delivery to address.

address.description: For 'order' with delivery: the full delivery address (5 characters or more).

details.description: The customer's own words: what they need (orders and quotes), or a note for a booking.

customer_phone.description: The customer's phone, ideally with country code; the business may call or WhatsApp them.

customer_email.description: Optional but recommended: Loomivo emails the customer when the business confirms or declines.

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.description: Check a request sent with create_request, by the ref it returned. Returns the status ('new' waiting for the business, 'confirmed', 'declined', 'cancelled', 'pending' waiting up to 24 hours, or 'not_available' if it expired), the time booked, the order total, the price for quotes, the business's note, and once confirmed how the customer pays the business. Use it to tell the customer whether the business confirmed. To cancel, use cancel_request. Read-only and safe to repeat; poll at most once a minute. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

tools.name: cancel_request
tools.description: Cancel a booking, order or quote request the customer sent with create_request, when the customer asks to cancel (to change a time or items: cancel, then send a new create_request). Needs the ref and, as proof it is the customer's own request, the phone number or email given in create_request. Works while the request is new, pending or confirmed; a declined, expired or already cancelled request can't be cancelled. Side effects: marks the request cancelled, frees the time or returns the items to stock, and tells the business by email and in its software. Always confirm with the customer before calling. Safe to repeat: a second call reports it is already cancelled. Errors: 'not_yours' (phone or email doesn't match), 'already_closed'. No sign-in or API key needed. Rate limit: 600 read calls and 60 create_request calls per hour per client IP; over the limit you get error -32000 'Too many requests' (wait, then retry).

contact.description: The customer's phone number or email, as given in create_request.
